findings: a disconnect longer than the ring buffer loses events with no gap marker anywhere: 2500 of 3400 never reached the server, and neither the stored run (seq numbers simply skip) nor the viewer has any way to know. Only session.stats().dropped knows, and nothing emits it.

retryIntervalMs defaults to 10s and there is no backoff ramp *down*: an app is blind for 9.99s after any blip, and at production rates that is more than the 2000-event ring buffer holds — so a blip on a busy run is data loss, not just delay.

checks.detail: 1.27x per-event cost — applyEvent copies the whole nodes record on every node lifecycle event, so cost per event rises with graph size

checks.name: layout of a realistic canvas (~800 nodes) stays under 50ms
per-node incremental layout cost does not blow up with canvas size
layout survives a 2000-deep chain (the documented ceiling)

findings: layout is ~O(n^2) in node count once the tree gets deep: 1.47ms at 269 nodes but 188.3ms at 3203. The shipped adapters keep node counts small (one node per distinct tool name), so this only bites imports and custom instrumentation with per-step node ids.

appendLayout costs 4x more per added node at 1763 nodes than at 300: it linear-scans every placed rectangle (and recomputes the bounding box) for each new node, so a long streaming run pays O(n^2) on the canvas while it is being watched.

tidyTreeLayout measures and places recursively, so a graph whose tree is deeper than ~6000 nodes overflows the stack and the canvas renders nothing. Unreachable with the shipped adapters (they use one stable `llm:step` node) but reachable from any custom instrumentation that mints a nodeId per step, and it degrades long before it crashes: 134.6ms per layout at depth 2000.
